backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, so grad accumulation halves). In a 300 s budget more optimizer steps usually help a small model.
backlog.title: Lower total batch to 2**18

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 (grad accum 1 with seq 2048 gives 131072 tokens). Many more steps in the fixed time; consider scaling MATRIX_LR by ~0.8 if unstable.
backlog.title: Lower total batch to 2**17

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.3 so more of the time is spent at full learning rate.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.3

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.7 to test a longer decay phase.
backlog.title: Warmdown ratio 0.7

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so the LR does not reach exactly zero at the end.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.05

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 to smooth early Muon and Adam updates, especially with the high embedding LR.
backlog.title: Short warmup

backlog.spec: Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05.
backlog.title: Matrix LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Raise EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.9.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.9

backlog.spec: Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.4

backlog.spec: Double UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008.
backlog.title: Unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Lower SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 to stabilise the per-layer scalars.
backlog.title: Scalar LR 0.25

backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1. In a short run, less decay may help fit.
backlog.title: Weight decay 0.1

backlog.spec: Keep WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2 at the start but scale it by the LR multiplier (or progress) so it decays toward 0 at the end of training.
backlog.title: Weight decay linearly decaying to zero

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.95).
backlog.title: Adam beta1 0.9

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.8, 0.99) for smoother second-moment estimates.
backlog.title: Adam beta2 0.99

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim 384*... by ASPECT_RATIO). A smaller model gets more steps in 300 s. Keep other settings.
backlog.title: Depth 6 wider-step model

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 32 if memory requires, to test a larger model against the time budget.
backlog.title: Depth 10

backlog.spec: Set ASPECT_RATIO = 80 with DEPTH 8 for a wider model (dim 640, head dim 128 gives 5 heads).
backlog.title: Aspect ratio 80

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 for more attention heads at the same width.
backlog.title: Head dim 64

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSL" or all "S" with a final L layer (e.g. "SSSS" plus the forced last full layer) to cut attention cost and gain more steps.
backlog.title: Window pattern SSSSL... shorter windows

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "L" to test whether full context everywhere beats the speed loss.
backlog.title: Window pattern all L

backlog.spec: Change the logit softcap value (likely 15) to 30, or remove it if present, in the forward pass.
backlog.title: Logit softcap tuning

backlog.spec: Change the Muon momentum schedule so it ramps to 0.97 over the first 100 steps and ends at 0.95 during warmdown, or adjust the existing ramp to be faster.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup shorter/higher

backlog.spec: Reduce Muon Newton-Schulz iterations from 5 to 4 if configurable to save time per step.
backlog.title: Muon NS steps 4

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP activation relu(x)^2 with a gated SiLU MLP with hidden size 8/3*dim rounded to a multiple of 64, to keep parameter count equal.
backlog.title: ReLU^2 to SwiGLU-style MLP

backlog.spec: If the model has value embeddings on alternating layers, remove them or apply them on all layers, to test the parameter and speed trade-off.
backlog.title: Disable value embeddings if present

backlog.spec: Add a small z-loss term 1e-4 * logsumexp(logits)^2 to the training loss only (not the evaluation call) to stabilise logits.
backlog.title: Dropout-free token smoothing: label smoothing 0.0 check via z-loss

backlog.spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before optimizer step, after unscaling.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine shape over the same WARMDOWN_RATIO of the time budget.
backlog.title: Time-based LR schedule with cosine warmdown

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown in the LR multiplier function with a cosine shape. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 and progress measured as elapsed training time over the 300 s budget. During warmdown, with p the fraction of the warmdown completed, use mult = FINAL_LR_FRAC + (1-FINAL_LR_FRAC)*0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)). Leave the flat phase unchanged. Only the multiplier function changes.
backlog.title: Cosine-shaped warmdown with time-based progress

backlog.spec: Keep an exponential moving average of all model parameters, decay 0.999, updated every optimizer step with torch._foreach_lerp_ on a copy of the params. Just before the final evaluation call, swap the EMA weights into the model, so the harness evaluates the averaged model. Do not touch the evaluation call or summary printing. Insert the swap just before them and nothing else near them. If EMA hurts because of the warmdown, lower the decay to 0.99.
backlog.title: Weight averaging (EMA) of parameters for evaluation

backlog.spec: If the model has per-layer scalars mixing the initial embedding x0 into the residual stream (resid_lambdas/x0_lambdas), raise the x0_lambda initialization from its current value to 0.3 and increase the SCALAR_LR for those to 0.5 (unchanged). If those scalars don't exist, add them: x = resid_lambda[i]*x + x0_lambda[i]*x0 before each block, with resid_lambda init 1.0 and x0_lambda init 0.2, stored as fp32 scalar params in the Adam scalar group.
backlog.title: Untie-free x0 residual mixing strengthened: learnable per-layer skip from embeddings

backlog.spec: For the first 30% of the time budget, train on sequences truncated to the first half of the context length. Reshape each batch (B,T) into (2B,T/2) by splitting each row in two, so the token count per step is unchanged. Switch to full-length rows afterwards. Sliding windows need no change. Use progress = elapsed time/300 to decide. This gives faster early steps because attention cost is lower. Be careful to compile-stable shapes: torch.compile will recompile once at the switch, which is acceptable, since compile time is not counted.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum: train short contexts first

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary term 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits.float(), dim=-1)**2) to the training loss only, never to the evaluation path. Compute it in the training forward, where logits are available after softcap. If the loss function is fused and does not expose logits, compute logsumexp from the logits tensor before cross_entropy. This stabilizes the logit scale.
backlog.title: Z-loss auxiliary regularizer on logits

backlog.spec: Bold Muon change: set the Muon update scale to max(1, rows/cols)**0.5 (if not already so) and multiply it by 0.2*sqrt(max(rows, cols)) to match AdamW RMS (the Moonlight scaling), then reduce MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.02 to compensate. Keep the other settings. This tests the RMS-matched update so that the same LR transfers across matrix shapes such as the MLP and attention projections.
backlog.title: Muon with Nesterov off and lr scaled by per-matrix shape

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 12 and ASPECT_RATIO = 43 so model_dim is about 512 (use 512 exactly, a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128 giving 4 heads). Keep everything else. Deeper and narrower models often trade steps for better per-token quality. If memory overflows at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, drop it to 32, which keeps TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE unchanged through grad accumulation.
backlog.title: Increase depth to 12 with narrower width

backlog.spec: Initialize lm_head weights with std 0.001 instead of the current value (or zero), and token embedding with std 0.5 instead of 1.0 if the current init is 1.0. Leave the other inits alone. Better-conditioned early logits reduce the initial loss spike and may improve the short-budget optimization. Change only init code in init_weights.
backlog.title: Untied embedding init scale and smaller lm_head init

backlog.spec: After the existing q/k RMS norm (add it if absent), multiply q by a fixed scale factor of 1.2 (equivalent to a sharper attention softmax). Make it a constant in the attention forward pass, applied to q only, before calling flash attention or SDPA. Keep the softmax_scale default. Sharper attention often helps short training runs with QK-norm.
backlog.title: QK-norm with learnable temperature and no-rope-free tweak: attention scale 1.2x

backlog.spec: Use the grad accumulation count to implement a batch ramp: for the first 25% of the time budget use half the micro-steps per optimizer step (an effective batch of 2**18), then switch to the full 2**19. Compute accum_steps each step from elapsed training time. Scale the loss by 1/accum_steps actually used. Keep the LR schedule unchanged. This gives more updates early, when gradients are noisy-tolerant.
backlog.title: Batch-size warmup: small batch early, full batch later

backlog.spec: Keep an exponential moving average copy of model parameters (decay 0.999, updated every optimizer step in float32 or bf16 under no_grad, using torch._foreach_lerp_). Before the final evaluation call, swap the EMA weights into the model (copy_ into params). Do not touch the evaluation call itself, only swap weights just before it. Memory cost is one extra copy of params, which is small for this model.
backlog.title: EMA of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary loss 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits.float(), dim=-1)**2) to the training loss only, when targets are given in training. Do not change the evaluation loss path. Implement it in the model forward only if it is the training path, e.g. by computing it in the training loop from a separately returned value, or by a flag that is off during eval.
backlog.title: Z-loss on logits

backlog.spec: Before the optimizer step, after accumulation of gradients, call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0). Keep everything else unchanged. If the loop has a place where grads for all micro-steps are summed, clip there once per optimizer step.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: Make Muon cautious weight decay follow the schedule: wd = WEIGHT_DECAY * (1 - progress), where progress is the time fraction of the training budget already used, updated each step in the same place where LR and momentum are scheduled. Keep the initial value at 0.2.
backlog.title: Weight decay linearly to zero

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSSSSSL" for the 8 layers, so only the last layer has full attention (the code always forces the last layer to be L). This gives cheaper attention and more steps in 300 s. Leave the window size definition unchanged.
backlog.title: Window pattern all-short with final long layer

backlog.spec: Start training with grad accumulation steps equal to 1 (about 2**16 tokens per step at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 and seq len 1024) and linearly increase accumulation to the full TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE value (2**19) over the first 25% of the time budget, rounding to integers. Scale the loss by the current accumulation count. Leave LR schedules as they are. This gives many more cheap early steps.
backlog.title: Batch size warmup

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**17 so each step uses a quarter of the tokens and the model takes about four times as many optimizer steps. Lower MATRIX_LR to 0.03 to compensate for the noisier gradients. With DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 and seq length 2048 or 1024, make sure the grad accumulation count is at least 1; if the per-device batch exceeds the total, reduce DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE accordingly.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch 2**17

backlog.spec: Replace relu^2 MLP with SwiGLU (hidden = 8/3*dim rounded to multiple of 64, gate and up projections plus down projection, down initialised to zero as the existing proj) and set DEPTH = 10 with ASPECT_RATIO 51 so model_dim rounds to 512 (4 heads of 128). Combine the two weakly helpful changes in one run.
backlog.title: SwiGLU plus depth 10 stack

backlog.spec: Set the Muon Newton-Schulz iteration count to 4 (from 5) to speed up the optimizer step and set WEIGHT_DECAY to 0.1. Both are small changes that leave the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Lower Muon NS steps to 4 and lower WD to 0.1

backlog.spec: Set WARMDOWN_RATIO to 0.65 and FINAL_LR_FRAC to 0.1 so the LR decays longer and ends at 10% of peak rather than zero. Leave all other hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.1 with warmdown 0.65

backlog.spec: Combine the three best weak signals in one run: replace the relu^2 MLP with SwiGLU (hidden = 8/3*dim rounded up to a multiple of 64, gate and up projections, down projection, same init scale as the old MLP), set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1, and set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18. Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: SwiGLU + WD 0.1 + batch 2**18 stack

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary loss 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits.float(), dim=-1)**2) to the training loss only (not to the evaluation path). Compute it from the same logits used for the cross-entropy, applied after the softcap. If the model's forward returns only the loss, add a training-only branch that computes the logits and both terms.
backlog.title: Z-loss on logits

backlog.spec: For the first 20% of the time budget use half the gradient accumulation steps (half the tokens per optimizer step, e.g. 2**18), then switch to the full 2**19. Scale nothing else. Gives more early optimizer steps while keeping the final large-batch quality. Make sure the loss normalisation divides by the actual number of micro-steps used.
backlog.title: Batch-size warmup

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN so that all layers use the short (half-context) window except the final layer, which is full. For depth 8 this is 'SSSSSSSL'. Check that the code forces the last layer to be long, and keep that behaviour. The saved attention compute should give more steps in 300 s.
backlog.title: Window pattern all-short except last layer

backlog.spec: Train the first 25% of the time budget on shorter contexts. Use the first 1/4 of each sequence by reshaping each batch from (B, T) to (4B, T/4) with the same token count, then switch to full length. Torch compile may recompile once on the shape change, which is fine. Keep the evaluation unchanged. Attention is cheaper early, so more steps fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum

backlog.spec: Initialise lm_head weights with std 0.001 (about 10x smaller than the current value), and raise UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008. This tests whether the output layer is under-trained in a short run.
backlog.title: Smaller lm_head init and unembedding LR 0.008

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 so the depth-8 model (dim 512) has 8 heads instead of 4. Keep the n_kv_head equal to the head count. Check that the flash-attention path supports head dim 64 and leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Head dim 64 with doubled heads

backlog.spec: Lower the Muon Newton-Schulz orthogonalisation iterations from 5 to 4 to cut optimizer overhead, and set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05 so the LR does not hit exactly zero at the end. Both changes are small and aim at more steps in the same time with a slightly softer finish.
backlog.title: Muon NS steps 4 with final LR fraction 0.05

memo:
Incumbent mean_adjusted 1.1145 over 16 runs; 15 slots logged, one aborted duplicate. Every single-run result so far was rejected. Gains of 0.0007 to 0.0030 are probably within noise.

Helped weakly: SwiGLU MLP (slot 3, 1.1115, -0.0030) was best. Lower WEIGHT_DECAY 0.1 (slot 13, -0.0020) and batch 2**18 (slot 4, -0.0015) came next. DEPTH 12 (-0.0014), ASPECT_RATIO 80 (-0.0010), DEPTH 6 (-0.0008), q scale 1.2 (-0.0007) and WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.3 (-0.0004) were marginal. Cosine decay was neutral.

Hurt: EMA 0.99 (+0.0275), WARMUP_RATIO 0.03 (+0.0115), faster momentum ramp (+0.0067), ADAM_BETAS (0.8, 0.99) (+0.0039), SCALAR_LR 0.25 (+0.0016), MATRIX_LR 0.05 (+0.0011).

Next: replicate SwiGLU to check it is real. Then stack SwiGLU, weight decay 0.1 and batch 2**18 in one run. Try lower MATRIX_LR and embedding LR. Avoid warmup, EMA, momentum and Adam-beta tweaks.
